description: Mercimek Corbasi is a beloved Turkish red lentil soup, known for its comforting warmth and rich, savory flavor. This hearty soup is a staple in Turkish cuisine, often enjoyed as a starter or a light meal. Its vibrant color and smooth texture make it a truly inviting dish that nourishes both body and soul.

instructions.title: Prepare Vegetables
instructions.text: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the finely chopped carrot and minced garlic, cooking for another 3-4 minutes until slightly tender.

instructions.title: Add Tomato Paste and Spices
instructions.text: Stir in the tomato paste, dried mint, and red pepper flakes. Cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, to toast the spices and deepen the flavor of the tomato paste.

instructions.title: Introduce Lentils and Broth
instructions.text: Add the rinsed red lentils to the pot. Pour in the vegetable or chicken broth. Season with salt and black pepper. Stir everything together well.

instructions.title: Simmer the Soup
instructions.text: Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and let it simmer for 25-30 minutes, or until the lentils are very tender and have broken down. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.

instructions.title: Blend for Smoothness
instructions.text: Carefully remove the pot from the heat. Using an immersion blender, blend the soup directly in the pot until it reaches a smooth, creamy consistency. Alternatively, transfer the soup in batches to a standard blender and blend until smooth (be cautious with hot liquids).

instructions.title: Adjust Consistency and Serve
instructions.text: Return the soup to the stove if needed to reheat gently. If the soup is too thick, you can add a little more hot broth or water until it reaches your desired consistency. Taste and adjust seasonings as necessary.

instructions.title: Garnish and Enjoy
instructions.text: Ladle the hot Mercimek Corbasi into bowls. Garnish with a sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley or mint, and serve immediately with lemon wedges on the side for squeezing. A drizzle of melted butter with extra red pepper flakes can be added for extra flavor.

tips: For an extra layer of flavor, prepare a 'nane tereyağı' (mint butter) by melting a tablespoon of butter with a pinch of dried mint and red pepper flakes, then drizzling it over the finished soup.
Always rinse your red lentils thoroughly until the water runs clear to remove any impurities and ensure a cleaner taste, preventing any murky appearance.
Mercimek Corbasi tastes even better the next day! Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days and reheat gently on the stovetop.
article:
Embark on a culinary journey to the heart of Turkey, where warmth, flavor, and tradition coalesce in a bowl of Mercimek Corbasi, the beloved Turkish Red Lentil Soup. This vibrant, comforting soup is more than just a dish; it's a staple found on nearly every Turkish table, from bustling city restaurants to cozy family homes. Known for its rich, earthy flavor, creamy texture, and incredible ease of preparation, Mercimek Corbasi offers a taste of authentic Turkish hospitality. Whether you're seeking a nutritious meal, a soothing antidote to a chilly day, or simply an exciting new recipe to master, this guide will walk you through everything you need to know to create your own perfect pot of this iconic soup. Get ready to awaken your senses with the aromatic spices and heartwarming goodness of Mercimek Corbasi.

## What is Mercimek Corbasi Red Lentil Soup?

Mercimek Corbasi (pronounced mer-jee-MEK chor-ba-su) is a traditional Turkish soup made primarily from red lentils. It's a cornerstone of Turkish cuisine, cherished for its simplicity, nourishing qualities, and distinctive flavor profile. Unlike some lentil soups that might be chunky, Mercimek Corbasi is typically pureed to a smooth, velvety consistency, making it incredibly comforting and easy to digest. The soup's signature color comes from the red lentils, which break down beautifully during cooking, creating a naturally thick and creamy base.

Culturally, Mercimek Corbasi holds a special place. It's often served as a starter to almost any meal, but it's equally popular as a light lunch or a comforting dinner on its own, especially during cooler months. Its appeal lies in its wholesome ingredients and the balance of savory, slightly tangy, and subtly spicy notes, often enhanced by a final drizzle of chili-infused butter and a squeeze of fresh lemon. This soup isn't just food; it’s a taste of home, a symbol of warmth and welcome that resonates deeply within Turkish culinary traditions.

## Ingredients You Need

Crafting an authentic Mercimek Corbasi requires a handful of simple, readily available ingredients. The magic lies in the quality of these components and how they come together to create a symphony of flavors.

*   **Red Lentils (1.5 cups):** The star of the show. Make sure they are split red lentils, as they cook faster and break down more easily for that signature creamy texture.
*   **Onion (1 medium):** Finely chopped, forms the aromatic base of the soup.
*   **Garlic (2-3 cloves):** Minced, adds depth and pungency.
*   **Tomato Paste (1 tablespoon):** Provides a rich umami flavor and a lovely reddish hue.
*   **Olive Oil (2 tablespoons):** For sautéing the aromatics. Butter can also be used for a richer flavor.
*   **Chicken or Vegetable Broth (6-7 cups):** Or water. Broth will yield a more flavorful soup.
*   **Dried Mint (1 teaspoon):** A crucial herb in Turkish cuisine, offering a distinctive refreshing note.
*   **Sweet Paprika (1 teaspoon):** For color and a mild, sweet pepper flavor.
*   **Cumin (1/2 teaspoon):** Adds warmth and earthiness, complementing the lentils beautifully.
*   **Salt and Black Pepper:** To taste.
*   **For the Chili-Mint Butter Drizzle (optional but highly recommended):**
    *   **Unsalted Butter (2 tablespoons):**
    *   **Red Pepper Flakes (Pul Biber) (1 teaspoon):** Or Aleppo pepper, for a gentle heat.
    *   **Dried Mint (1/2 teaspoon):**
*   **Fresh Lemon Wedges:** For serving, essential for brightening the soup's flavors.

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Making Mercimek Corbasi is straightforward, even for novice cooks. Follow these steps for a perfect pot every time:

1.  **Prepare the Lentils:** Rinse the red lentils thoroughly under cold running water until the water runs clear. This removes any starch and impurities. Drain well.
2.  **Sauté Aromatics:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat the olive oil (or butter) over medium heat. Add the finely chopped onion and sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.
3.  **Build the Flavor Base:** Stir in the tomato paste, sweet paprika, and cumin. Cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, allowing the spices to bloom and the tomato paste to deepen in color and flavor.
4.  **Add Lentils and Liquid:** Add the rinsed and drained red lentils to the pot, stirring to coat them with the aromatic mixture. Pour in the chicken or vegetable broth (or water). Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are completely tender and have started to break down. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
5.  **Blend Until Smooth:** Remove the pot from the heat. Using an immersion blender, carefully blend the soup directly in the pot until it is completely smooth and creamy. If you don't have an immersion blender, transfer the soup in batches to a regular blender (be cautious with hot liquids – fill only halfway, cover with a towel, and vent the lid) and blend until smooth, then return to the pot.
6.  **Season and Finish:** Stir in the dried mint. Season the Mercimek Corbasi generously with salt and black pepper to taste. If the soup is too thick, add a little more hot broth or water until it reaches your desired consistency. Heat gently for a few more minutes.
7.  **Prepare the Drizzle (Optional but Recommended):** While the soup is simmering or just before serving, melt the unsalted butter in a small pan over medium-low heat. Once melted, add the red pepper flakes (pul biber) and the remaining dried mint. Sizzle for about 30 seconds until fragrant, being careful not to burn the spices.
8.  **Serve:** Ladle the hot Mercimek Corbasi into bowls. Drizzle each serving generously with the chili-mint butter and serve immediately with fresh lemon wedges on the side.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

Achieving that authentic, comforting flavor for your Mercimek Corbasi is all about a few key details:

*   **Rinse Your Lentils:** Don't skip this step! Rinsing helps remove excess starch, which can make your soup cloudy, and ensures a cleaner flavor.
*   **Bloom Your Spices:** Cooking the tomato paste, paprika, and cumin for a minute or two with the aromatics before adding liquid helps to release their full flavor and aroma, deepening the soup's profile.
*   **Blend Thoroughly:** For that signature velvety texture, ensure your soup is blended until completely smooth. No grainy bits allowed! An immersion blender makes this incredibly easy.
*   **The Power of Lemon:** A squeeze of fresh lemon juice just before eating is non-negotiable. It brightens the soup, cuts through the richness, and elevates all the flavors.
*   **Don't Skip the Drizzle:** While optional, the chili-mint butter drizzle (often called *nane yağı* or *pul biberli tereyağı*) adds a crucial layer of flavor, aroma, and visual appeal that defines traditional Mercimek Corbasi. It introduces a gentle heat and fragrant herbal note that transforms the soup.
*   **Adjust Consistency:** Red lentil soup can thicken as it cools. If reheating, you might need to add a splash of hot water or broth to reach your preferred consistency.

## Serving Suggestions

Mercimek Corbasi is incredibly versatile and can be enjoyed in various ways:

*   **Classic Starter:** Serve it as the first course to any Turkish meal, alongside fresh bread and perhaps some olives or pickles.
*   **Light Lunch or Dinner:** It's hearty enough to be a meal on its own, especially when paired with crusty bread or pita bread for dipping.
*   **With a Side of Salad:** A simple green salad with a light vinaigrette makes a refreshing accompaniment.
*   **Garnish:** Beyond the chili-mint butter and lemon, you can also garnish with a sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley or a few extra red pepper flakes for those who enjoy more heat.
*   **Alongside Kebabs or Rice Dishes:** The soup’s comforting nature makes it a perfect counterpoint to richer main courses.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Mercimek Corbasi recipe is perfect as is, you can certainly experiment with variations to suit your taste or dietary needs:

*   **Vegetarian/Vegan:** The recipe is naturally vegetarian. To make it vegan, simply use vegetable broth instead of chicken broth and olive oil instead of butter for sautéing. For the drizzle, use extra virgin olive oil instead of butter.
*   **Add Vegetables:** For extra nutrients and body, you can add finely diced carrots or potatoes along with the lentils. They will cook down and blend seamlessly into the soup. A small amount of red bell pepper can also add a subtle sweetness.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the amount of red pepper flakes in the butter drizzle to control the heat. For a spicier soup, you can even add a pinch of cayenne pepper to the pot along with the other spices.
*   **Different Herbs:** While dried mint is traditional and highly recommended, you could experiment with a pinch of dried oregano or thyme if you wish, though it will alter the classic Turkish flavor profile.
*   **Creaminess Boost:** For an even creamier texture, some recipes call for adding a small amount of milk or cream at the very end, after blending. However, traditional Mercimek Corbasi achieves its creaminess solely from the lentils.

Mercimek Corbasi is more than just a soup; it's an embrace in a bowl, a testament to the power of simple ingredients creating profound flavor. This nourishing, flavorful, and incredibly satisfying Turkish red lentil soup is waiting to become a cherished recipe in your kitchen. Enjoy the journey of making and savoring this magnificent culinary delight!
